comparator.name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
comparator.route: Six DSAI electives in the 36-EC free-choice space
comparator.sourceNotes: The live 2026-2027 Leiden Study Guide establishes a complete 180-EC programme: 120 EC of mandatory courses across Years 1 and 2; 24 EC of mandatory Year 3 components, consisting of AI and Ethics (3 EC), Software Engineering (6 EC) and the Bachelor Thesis Project (15 EC); and 36 EC of elective space. The standard discipline-specific route of six DSAI electives is selected rather than a 30-EC minor plus one DSAI elective because it most directly continues the programme's broad academic identity. The six choices remain an explicit restricted-choice aggregate rather than invented individual selections.
components: Six 6-EC courses selected from the published third-year DSAI elective list; the aggregate choice space is preserved without inventing individual selections.

routeSelection.route: Six DSAI electives in the 36-EC free-choice space
routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor allows either six DSAI electives or a 30-EC minor plus one DSAI elective. The six-DSAI-elective route most directly continues the programme's defining data-science, artificial-intelligence, computing and cognition curriculum, independently of UCR fit. Individual elective choices remain uninstantiated because the official curriculum defines a genuine restricted-choice space.

core: Programming, software engineering, databases and computer systems
Algorithms, data structures and computational problem-solving for intelligent systems
Mathematical foundations: calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics and inference
Data science, machine learning, neural computing, data analysis, visualisation and prediction
Artificial-intelligence reasoning, symbolic AI, reinforcement learning and intelligent-system design
Research methods, interdisciplinary project work, responsible data use and an independent bachelor thesis
adjacent: Human cognition, cognitive neuroscience and computational models of information processing
Human interaction with intelligent systems and ethical, responsible AI
Data visualisation and scientific discovery from complex data
Embodied, autonomous and conversational intelligent agents
Language, media and interaction in computational systems
questions: How do human and artificial intelligence process information, learn and interact?
How can data-driven intelligent systems be designed, evaluated and used responsibly?

trace: teaches research design, operationalization, experimental design and sampling together with descriptive and inferential statistics; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the study of experiments, observational data, bias and summary statistics that Leiden's Principles of Data Science treats

examines AI fairness and bias, privacy, responsibility, the moral status of AI systems and the philosophical and psychological questions about human-AI interaction; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the philosophical issues raised by AI that Leiden University treats in Philosophy & Artificial Intelligence

teaches planning for AI systems in deterministic and non-deterministic environments with uncertainty, partial observability and optimisation under constraints; it directly implements the planning and decision-making under uncertainty strand of the core, treated by Leiden University in Reasoning Techniques and Operations Research

covers logic, discrete mathematics, patterns and structures with applications to computer science and algorithm construction; it directly implements the discrete-mathematics and logic foundation of the core

covers uninformed and informed search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction and convex, linear and non-linear optimisation by rational agents with laboratory work; it directly implements the search and optimisation methods of Leiden's Reasoning Techniques

teaches reinforcement-learning frameworks and algorithms and has students build agents with neural networks that learn by trial and error; it directly implements the behaviour-learning agents of Leiden's Intelligent Systems
introduces relational database theory, SQL, normalization and query processing; it directly implements the database content of the core

teaches software planning, requirements gathering, testing, quality assurance, maintenance and code review through projects in C++ and Haskell; it directly implements the software-engineering strand of the core
teaches algorithm design and analysis, data structures and experimental performance analysis with laboratory work; it directly implements the algorithms and data-structures strand of the core

studies modern algebraic algorithms and solution methods for optimisation problems with algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the algorithmic problem-solving and optimisation content that Leiden's core addresses in graph theory, algorithms and linear programming

teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation, including spatial and text data, and ends with an own research project analysing data; it directly implements the data-science process of exploring and preparing data that Leiden's introductory data-science course and Data Analysis address

teaches linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering on real data; it directly implements the machine-learning strand of the core

teaches camera and image models, feature detection and the processing, analysis and understanding of image data with programming; it makes a specific complementary contribution as a data-science application of machine learning to visual data, the territory of Leiden's image and video processing elective

builds neural networks from scratch and in TensorFlow, applies them to vision and text and studies large language models; it directly implements the deep-learning side of machine learning and the neural-language-model content that Leiden University addresses in Natural Language Processing

treats kinematics, motion and manipulation of autonomous robots and the computational problems they raise; it makes a specific complementary contribution to intelligent agents acting in physical environments, which Leiden's Intelligent Systems treats with robots as an agent type

teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging, and elements of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving; it directly implements the programming foundation of the core, which Leiden University teaches in Procedural Programming and Objects in Programming
teaches differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations through projects; it directly implements the calculus foundation of the mathematical core
teaches matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations; it directly implements the linear-algebra foundation of the mathematical core and of machine learning

teaches numerical methods for root finding, differentiation and differential equations with attention to algorithm accuracy; it directly implements the numerical-methods strand of the mathematical core

extends calculus to several dimensions and differential equations with computer algebra software for data analysis; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the multivariable calculus underlying optimisation and neural-network training

characterises linear time-invariant systems through impulse and frequency response, convolution, Fourier representations and transfer functions; it directly implements the dynamical-systems side of mathematical modelling taught in Leiden's Mathematical Modelling
covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; it directly implements the probability-and-statistics foundation of the core

introduces central themes of Western philosophy on knowledge, consciousness and responsibility, their relation to computer science and psychology and the methods of philosophical argument; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the philosophical foundation for the philosophy-of-science and philosophy-of-AI content of the programme

examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and practical ethics; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the ethical theory needed to analyse the moral questions raised by intelligent systems

asks whether the mind can be explained neurobiologically and whether artificial systems, including large language models, can be conscious; it directly implements the philosophical issues about replicating human consciousness and intelligence that Leiden University treats in Philosophy & Artificial Intelligence

explores the neural mechanisms of perception and action and how the brain guides goal-directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience; it directly implements the perception and action topics of the cognitive-neuroscience strand

deepens neurophysiology and experimental cognitive neuroscience and treats memory, attention, executive function, emotion, social cognition and decision making; it directly implements the learning, memory and decision topics of cognitive neuroscience, which Leiden University includes among the cognitive models relevant to knowledge engineering

examines how people acquire, produce and understand language, with the neuroscience of language, experimental approaches and links to computer science; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the human counterpart of the computational language processing in Leiden's Natural Language Processing

introduces functional brain anatomy, neuronal communication and the psychological and neuroscientific study of perception, learning and behaviour; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the cognitive and biological psychology that Leiden University teaches in Computational and Cognitive Neuroscience, without covering its modelling of cognition

teaches multivariate statistical models, regression, logistic regression, factor analysis and experimental methods; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the applied data analysis (multiple regression, classification and dimensionality reduction) of Leiden's Data Analysis

alternatives.label: Data Science & Artificial Intelligence: Computing, Mathematics & Machine Learning
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines programming, computer science, mathematics, statistics, data science, machine learning and AI reasoning; the label names those dominant strands without implying Leiden's full specialist sequence.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines programming and software, algorithms and databases, a substantial mathematics-and-statistics spine, data science and machine learning, and AI reasoning, optimisation and reinforcement learning.
progression: Introduction to Programming and Logic & Discrete Mathematics open semester 1 and precede every dependent course; Mathematical Methods (semester 2) precedes Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Neural Networks & Deep Learning; Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics and Algorithms & Data Structures (semester 3) precede Software Development, Advanced Algorithms (semester 4) and Machine Learning, Decision-making in AI (semester 5); Machine Learning (semester 5) precedes Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Optimization Methods in AI and Reinforcement Learning (semester 6); the brain-and-behaviour gateway is taken in semester 5 as a stand-alone course with no dependent course.

alternatives.label: Cognition, Human–AI Interaction & Responsible Intelligent Systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines cognitive science, neuroscience, philosophy and ethics with machine learning, robotics and AI decision-making; the label states that human-and-artificial-intelligence emphasis directly.
alternatives.concept: This route takes Leiden's cognition-and-computation strand as its organising logic, combining cognitive neuroscience, language, philosophy of mind and AI ethics with machine learning, intelligent agents, robotics and data analysis.
progression: Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science and Introduction to Brain & Behavior open semester 1; Mathematical Methods and Perception & Action (semester 2) follow their gateways; Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics and Machine Learning (semester 3) precede Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Optimization Methods in AI and Robotics (semester 4) and Decision-making in AI, Reinforcement Learning and Image Processing & Computer Vision (semesters 5 and 6); Higher Order Functions (semester 5) and Psycholinguistics (semester 6) follow the brain-and-behaviour gateway and Perception & Action; Introduction to Western Philosophy (semester 5) precedes Philosophy of Mind (semester 6), while Ethics (semester 4) has no prerequisite.
alternatives.distinctness: The closest match prioritises the broad technical computing, mathematics, software and data-science sequence. This route instead makes cognition, language, philosophy, ethics and embodied intelligent systems central, replacing seven specialist computing and mathematics courses with cognitive-science, philosophy, ethics and robotics courses. The alternatives share 17 of 24 courses and differ by 7 courses (52.5 EC), so they exceed the 30-EC / four-course floor for reasons that follow from the distinct organising concept.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the nine generator-eligible interests defining the technical data-science and AI core. The seven remaining generator-eligible interests form one coherent cognition, human-intelligence, interaction and responsible-AI direction and support a second feasible programme that differs by seven courses. After that inclusion, no unowned generator-eligible direction remains to justify a third programme; support-only curricular topics cannot generate one independently.

Both teach algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis.
Both cover relational databases, SQL, data modelling and normalization.
Both develop software through requirements, design, testing, maintenance and quality assurance.
Both provide formal logic and discrete structures for computational reasoning; the UCR course integrates these with algorithm construction.

Data science, machine learning & intelligent systems
Both orient students to data preparation, analysis and intelligent-system questions through practical work.
Both teach regression, classification, clustering and evaluation of predictive models.
Both develop neural-network models and apply them to complex data.
Both cover symbolic problem solving, search and reasoning for artificial intelligence.
Both study agents that learn behaviour through reinforcement.
Both connect perception and action to embodied agents, though Leiden concentrates on conversational-agent design.
Both study cognitive processes and computational accounts of information processing.
Both examine language processing and its relationship to computational systems.
No selected UCR course reproduces Leiden's dedicated technical security component.
Both examine fairness, responsibility, privacy and ethical questions raised by artificial intelligence.
Both develop research design, operationalisation, experiments, sampling and statistical inference.

Leiden's separate advanced Software Engineering component has no remaining one-to-one UCR counterpart after Software Development is aligned in Year 2.
UCR has no scheduled bachelor-thesis course; the standardized optional independent research element is placed against this component.
Leiden's genuine 36-EC DSAI elective space is preserved without inventing individual choices.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial programming, mathematics, statistics, machine learning and artificial intelligence. Leiden additionally provides a fixed specialist sequence in computer systems, formal computer-science foundations, security, language and computation, software engineering, an independent thesis and 36 EC of advanced DSAI electives. UCR can combine related courses but does not reproduce that full sequence.

Leiden organises Data Science and Artificial Intelligence as a fixed specialist bachelor with a large advanced elective space. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across computer science, mathematics, data science, artificial intelligence, cognitive science and philosophy.
